The dotnet build of the full solution (needed before the historical-simulation replay can run) did not complete: it reproducibly hangs while compiling QuantConnect.Common across four independent attempts and four different mitigations, with no OOM, cgroup throttling, or disk-wait state observed. Historical-simulation could not be run on this root; reported as a blocker, not silently skipped or worked around.

conclusion: Four attempts, four independent mitigations, one fully automated (non-operator-judged) timeout confirmation. Stopping here rather than continuing an open-ended diagnostic campaign; reporting LEAN historical-simulation as blocked on this host for this session.

diagnostic_evidence.referenced_package_dlls_valid: Spot-checked cloneextensions/fasterflect/sharpziplib/mathnet.numerics/mcmaster.extensions.commandlineutils DLLs referenced by Common's compile response file: all valid PE32 .NET assemblies, plausible sizes, not truncated/corrupt.
diagnostic_evidence.memory: MemAvailable stayed >= 8 GiB before every attempt; cgroup memory.current never exceeded ~1.1 GiB of a 6 GiB memory.max; memory.events high/max/oom all stayed 0.
diagnostic_evidence.cpu: cgroup cpu.max ~2200000/100000 (about 22 cores, unthrottled); cpu.stat nr_throttled stayed 0 across the whole job.
diagnostic_evidence.disk: No process observed in D (uninterruptible disk sleep) state during any attempt.
diagnostic_evidence.consistent_reproduction_point: All four attempts reached the identical point: the three small, fast projects (Logging, Configuration, Compression) always complete in seconds; the hang begins immediately after QuantConnect.Common's CoreCompile writes its MSBuild cache files and starts csc.

limitations: This is an environment/tooling blocker report, not a completed native LEAN historical-simulation E2E on the new root.
